Dr. Isha Arora

Understanding gas–liquid systems.

From dispersion-scale measurements to dynamic models of generation and stability.

I am a Chemical Engineering PhD working on colloidal gas aphrons: surfactant-stabilized gas microbubbles, their generation, gas holdup, and stability.

Explore my research
Colloidal gas aphronsGas–liquid dispersionsInterfacial phenomenaModelling + experiments
A closer look

The system I study

Colloidal gas aphrons are surfactant-stabilized gas microbubbles. Microscopy captures the dispersion; structural schematics describe the proposed interfacial organization.

Experiments + modelling

Connecting what we observe with what we predict.

I study how generation mode and operating conditions influence dispersion volume, gas holdup, and stability. Dynamic models provide a way to interpret how the system evolves over time.

Microscopy complements these measurements by revealing the appearance and size variation of the microbubbles.

Inside my research

How do operating conditions and flow configuration influence the formation and evolution of a gas–liquid dispersion? My doctoral research approached this question through complementary models and measurements.

01 / Generation

Colloidal gas aphrons

Experimental investigation of surfactant-stabilized gas dispersions produced in rotating-disc generators, examining generation behaviour under different operating configurations.

What I investigate

I compare batch, continuous-flow, semi-batch, and recirculation modes to understand how operating configuration influences the generation and evolution of the dispersion.

02 / Dynamics

Mathematical modelling

Coupled nonlinear ordinary differential equations describing the evolution of gas and liquid in continuous-flow systems, with experimental and numerical validation.

How the model works

The model follows gas and liquid evolution through coupled balances. Experimental measurements test whether its predicted trends describe the behaviour of the continuous-flow generator.

03 / Stability

Recirculation and gas holdup

Investigation of batch and recirculation operation, assessing how recycling affects dispersion volume, gas holdup, and stability over time.

Why recirculation matters

Recycling provides another way to influence dispersion behaviour. My experiments compare volume, gas holdup, and stability between batch and batch-recirculation operation.

  • Dynamic modelling
  • Gas holdup measurements
  • Optical microscopy
  • Image analysis
  • Experimental validation

About me

I recently completed my PhD in Chemical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, under the supervision of Prof. Ashok N. Bhaskarwar. My doctoral work combined mathematical modelling with experimental investigation of colloidal gas aphron generation across batch, continuous-flow, semi-batch, and recirculation modes.

I am interested in connecting measurable dispersion behaviour with the fluid-mechanical and interfacial processes that govern gas incorporation and stability.

Doctoral thesis
Mathematical Modeling of the Generation of Colloidal Gas Aphrons
